title: TikTok: politics for young people. What are Trump and Milei talking about? Polarization, hate and misinformation in election campaigns
screen_reason: Quantitative content analysis of 200 TikTok videos (100 Donald Trump / United States 2024, 100 Javier Milei / Argentina 2023). Videos were coded on a binary scale against an explicit mis/disinformation typology (Wardle & Derakhshan 2017; Tirado Garcia & Alonso-Munoz 2024): joke/satire/parody, exaggeration, decontextualisation, fabricated content, video manipulation, video reuse. The paper reports the share of videos in each candidate's 100-video corpus carrying each disinformation element, with a clear denominator, so it yields CONTENT estimates. Note: no single overall '% of videos that are misinformation' is reported; every row is one of the paper's disinformation subvariables.

estimates.denominator: 100 TikTok videos in which Donald Trump is the protagonist, published in the six months before the 5 November 2024 election, retrieved purposively via #trump2024, #donaldtrump, #trumpsupport
estimates.definition: Video coded 1 on subvariable V.5.4 'Contenido fabricado' (completely fabricated content) of the paper's disinformation variable

estimates.ground_truth_detail: The two authors coded 100 videos each (one candidate each) on a binary nominal scale (1 = attribute present, 0 = absent) using the disinformation typology of Tirado Garcia & Alonso-Munoz (2024) and Wardle & Derakhshan (2017); the analysis was repeated at different times and the authors swapped their video sets to check category consistency, with reliability estimated at 94 % (no kappa reported).
estimates.moderator_quote: El análisis se ha hecho en 200 vídeos (N = 200) publicados durante los seis meses de campaña anteriores al día de las respectivas elecciones: 100 por cada candidato (n1 = 100 y n2 = 100). La selección se ha hecho en base a que el candidato fuera el protagonista del vídeo y que este tuviera contenido referido a la campaña y los temas de la campaña.
estimates.notes: English translation of the sentence this value comes from: 'Trump uses it in 2 % of the videos analysed and Milei uses it in 5 %.' This is the strictest veracity category in the paper and is treated here as the base row for the US cell; the other US rows are broader definition variants of the same 100-video denominator. Percentages are stated verbatim in the prose (the accompanying Grafico 4 is an image and was not read). The sentence as printed in the article reads: «El contenido completamente fabricado es menos frecuente en los discursos de ambos candidatos. missed_or_uncertain: 1) NO overall headline number exists: the paper never reports a single '% of videos containing disinformation'. Every row above is one of the seven V.5 subvariables, and they are not mutually exclusive, so they must NOT be summed (R8 forbids cross-category sums in any case). 2) Trump's manipulation and reuse rates are given only qualitatively ('Trump no lo hace apenas'), so no US rows for those two variants. 3) Hate-speech and polarisation percentages were NOT extracted because they are outside the review's misinformation construct: hate speech present in 17 % of Trump videos and 0 % of Milei videos; attacks on the adversary 45 % (Trump) / 42 % (Milei); political promises 52 % / 30 %; threats 4 % / 34 %; defence against attacks 3 % / 20 %; intention to help the receiver 36 % (Trump); 56 % of Milei videos attack 'la casta'. 4) Audience figures (Trump 95 % / Milei 92 % addressing the general public; Milei 14 % directly addressing young people) are not misinformation measures. 5) Figures the paper cites from other sources were excluded per R8: 'en Argentina el 76 % considera que la desinformacion debilita el proceso electoral y el 70 % que aumenta la polarizacion politica (Martinez, 2023)' [in Argentina 76 % consider that disinformation weakens the electoral process and 70 % that it increases political polarisation]; Gallup 2024 media-trust 32 %; TikTok penetration 76 % of US 18-24s, 46 % of Argentines. 6) Four bar charts (Graficos 1-4) are images in the source text and could not be read; all values used here are stated verbatim in the running prose. 7) denom_selection was coded single_source because each 100-video corpus is defined by one political actor as protagonist; a defensible alternative is 'curated', since selection was hashtag-driven and spans several accounts (Milei had no official TikTok account during the campaign).

rob.design: Purposive ('recoleccion intencionada') hashtag-driven sample of 200 TikTok videos, 100 per candidate, published in the six months of campaign before each election (US 5 Nov 2024; Argentina 22 Oct / 19 Nov 2023); inclusion required the candidate to be the video's protagonist and the content to relate to the campaign. Seven variables and 34 subvariables coded on a binary nominal scale (1 present / 0 absent). Each author coded one candidate's 100 videos, repeated the coding at different times, and then swapped video sets to check category consistency; reliability 'estimada en el 94 %' with no kappa, no independent coders and no per-variable agreement reported. No sampling frame size, no response rate applicable, no confidence intervals. Content and discourse analysis combined.
